claude_content_type.description: Discriminator for a content block. Matches the Anthropic wire format; unknown values deserialize as UNDEFINED and are skipped downstream.

claude_task_budget_type.description: Unit a task budget is denominated in. The API defines exactly one.

claude_service_tier.description: Which tier actually served a request, as reported on every response (verified against api.anthropic.com 2026-08-11: a plain call reports `standard`, a batched one reports `batch`). Load-bearing for cost: a batch reports RAW, undiscounted token counts, so anything pricing a response off token counts alone over-reports a batched call by 2x.

claude_batch_processing_status.description: Lifecycle of a whole batch. `ended` means every request reached a terminal state -- succeeded, errored, canceled or expired -- NOT that they all succeeded.

claude_batch_result_type.description: Terminal state of ONE request inside a batch. Every one of the four is reachable on a batch that ended, so a caller reconciling results has to handle all of them: `expired` in particular is what a request that never ran within 24 hours comes back as.

fields.name: ttl
fields.description: How long an entry written at this breakpoint stays readable: "5m" or "1h". Omitted means the API default of 5 minutes. A string rather than an enum because apibuilder's Scala generator names the case object after the wire value, and neither value is a legal Scala identifier; the type-safe choice lives on AiRequest.cacheTtl instead, which is the surface callers actually use.

claude_tool.description: A tool the model may call. input_schema is the JSON schema for the tool's arguments; strict guarantees the model's input validates against it.

claude_output_config.description: Output controls. effort tunes thinking depth and token spend; format constrains the response to a JSON schema (replaces the deprecated top-level output_format); task_budget tells the model how much of max_tokens it should plan to spend.

claude_task_budget.description: Advisory token ceiling the model is made aware of while generating. The server injects a countdown marker, so the model paces itself and wraps up gracefully instead of being truncated at max_tokens -- which is an enforced ceiling the model never sees. Requires the task-budgets-2026-03-13 beta header.

fields.name: total
fields.description: Tokens the model may plan to spend on this turn. Minimum accepted by the API is 20,000; anything lower is rejected.

claude_api_output_format.description: Structured output configuration for guaranteed JSON schema compliance

fields.name: schema
fields.description: JSON schema object defining the structure

claude_content_block.description: One content block on a message or response. A single flat model spanning all block types (discriminated on type) rather than a union, because a spec that has both a union and error-response mustParse handling hits a known bryzek-generator ambiguous-implicit compile error. Wire JSON is identical to the union form; only the populated fields differ by type: text -> text; tool_use -> id, name, input; tool_result -> tool_use_id, content, is_error; thinking -> thinking, signature; redacted_thinking -> data; image -> source; document -> source. Retain every field verbatim when echoing assistant content back, or the API rejects the modified block.

fields.name: service_tier
fields.description: Tier that served this request. Optional only because a response recorded before this field existed does not carry one; the live API sets it on every response. Anything computing cost MUST read it -- see claude_service_tier.

claude_cache_creation.description: cache_creation_input_tokens split by the TTL each write was made at. Without this split a 1h write (2x input) is indistinguishable from a 5m one (1.25x) and any cost rollup over the total under-reports it -- which is exactly the direction that would hide a longer TTL that stopped paying for itself.

claude_batch_form.description: Body of a batch submission. The API caps a batch at 100,000 requests or 256 MB, whichever comes first.

claude_batch_request_item.description: One request in a batch. `custom_id` is the ONLY way a result is matched back to its caller: results are returned in ARBITRARY order (verified 2026-08-11 -- a batch submitted a, b, c came back c, b, a), so never key by position. `params` is a full Messages request, minus the two things a batch rejects: `fallbacks` and fast mode.

claude_batch_request_counts.description: How the batch's requests are distributed across terminal states. While processing_status is in_progress these move; once it is ended, `processing` is 0 and the rest sum to the batch size.

claude_batch.description: A submitted batch. `results_url` is null until processing_status is `ended`; asking for results before then is an error, not an empty list.

fields.name: expires_at
fields.description: 24 hours after creation. Anything still processing at this point comes back as an `expired` result -- the hard ceiling on batch latency.

claude_batch_result.description: One line of the JSONL results body -- see claude_batch_result_detail for why this is not fetched through the generated client.

claude_batch_result_detail.description: Outcome of one request. A flat model discriminated on `type` rather than a union, for the reason documented on claude_content_block. Populated by type: succeeded -> message; errored -> error; canceled and expired populate NEITHER, so a caller that reads `message.get` on anything but `succeeded` will throw on the two states that mean the batch ran out of time or was called off.

claude_batch.description: The Message Batches API: the same Messages surface at 50% of the token price, run asynchronously. Three of its four operations are ordinary JSON and generated here. The fourth -- GET /v1/messages/batches/:id/results, which carries the actual payload -- returns `application/x-jsonl` rather than JSON, which apibuilder has no response type for, so it is fetched by hand (see ClaudeBatchResults in lib-ai) and its lines parsed as claude_batch_result.

operations.description: Best-effort cancellation. Requests already in flight are allowed to finish, so a canceled batch generally ends with a mix of `succeeded` and `canceled` results rather than all `canceled`.
